facts.text: Every one of the seven reviewers should receive a one-page credibility map showing every safety claim, whether its evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, the real-world data that validated the supporting simulation model, the remaining uncertainty, and who has authority to accept that residual uncertainty.

facts.text: The one-page credibility map recommended for all seven reviewers applies NASA and ASME credibility principles to the collision mitigation validation program.

facts.text: No reviewer should be asked to approve virtual testing as a category; reviewers should instead approve specific substitutions of validated simulation models for defined repetitive physical tests.

facts.text: Each proposed substitution of simulation for physical testing should specify the machine, sensor, configuration and environment envelope within which a validated model may replace a defined repetitive physical test, and identify the boundary tests that remain physical.

facts.text: Approving specific simulation-for-physical-test substitutions rather than virtual testing as a broad category prevents a broad management commitment from outrunning the evidence.
